description: IBM is a cornerstone of U.S. business that is best known for its software, cloud computing services, and consulting. Incorporated in 1911, and later rebranded as International Business Machines, the company has ridden the many waves of innovation over the decades, from early technology such as tabulating machines, and time clocks for employee punch-ins, to today’s advancements in artificial intelligence. As of 2024, it was among just a few dozen companies to have appeared on the Fortune 500 every year since the list’s inception in 1955.

title: International Business Machines

rankings.title: Fortune 50 AI Innovators
rankings.itemDescription: Big Blue, based in Armonk, N.Y., was early to the AI game with Watson, which was first introduced over two decades ago, mesmerizing the world with what the tech could do. In 2023, the company launched its generative AI offerings, called Watsonx, with the conviction that the technology will bring about a productivity boom. CEO Arvind Krishna expects close to a third of current roles at the company can be taken over by AI and automation in the next five years, freeing up human staff for high-value work. The benefits from boosting productivity could mean reinvestment and larger margins, Krishna suggested. For its part, IBM’s Watsonx already has clients like NASA and Wix on board. The company also brings AI to clients to assist them with automation, modernization, and providing customer care services. For instance, Brazilian bank Bradesco automated its customer service answers using Watson Assistant, responding to 283,000 questions monthly. IBM is focusing on expanding the use of its AI where it is scalable and relevant, while strengthening its position beyond a legacy IT business; it has committed to training 2 million people in AI over the next three years. It acquired software company Apptio in a $4.6 billion deal to complement its AI portfolio and Red Hat cloud business.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription:
Information technology company IBM delivered $60.5 billion in total revenue in 2022, with its hybrid cloud unit accounting for $22.4 billion of that sum.

  • Still, sales growth stagnated at the end of 2022, and IBM said it would cut about 3,900 jobs.

  • In May 2023, IBM said it would give $100 million to the University of Chicago and the University of Tokyo to aid in the building of a quantum-centric supercomputer within a decade.

  • A longtime A.I. leader, IBM stepped into the current ChatGPT-inspired frenzy in May 2023 by unveiling Watsonx, a platform that offers tools for building A.I. models and access to pretrained models that can generate code and text.

rankings.title: Change the World
rankings.itemDescription: To help businesses adapt to climate-change-related disruptions, IBM recently launched its Environmental Intelligence Suite, software-as-a-service incorporating an extensive weather data set with powerful A.I. EIS is already being used by freight giant Norfolk Southern to fight freezes on rail lines, and by Brazilian biofuel maker BP Bunge Bioenergía to forecast high-risk areas for wildfires.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: IBM generated $57.4 billion in revenue from continuing operations in 2021, up from $55.17 billion in 2020. That’s not enormous growth, but it’s a step in the right direction for a company that has been coping for a decade with declining revenue from the IT-management and hardware businesses that used to be at its core. CEO Arvind Krishna has been working to bolster IBM’s presence in cloud software, business automation, and artificial intelligence. The company has recently won plaudits for its Environmental Intelligence Suite, an A.I.-powered system designed to help other companies manage their CO2 emissions and predict and prepare for climate-related threats.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: Big Blue was under new leadership in 2020 after Arvind Krishna took over for Ginni Rometty as CEO just after the pandemic shut down IBM offices around the world. Adding some of the most rigorous safety measures, IBM has not had a single known case of workplace transmission of COVID-19. The company also offered additional weeks of paid emergency leave for employees dealing with the pandemic and backup child and elder care options. IBM also joined with the U.S. government and other researchers attacking COVID-19 and provided free access to its supercomputers. IBM also reached out to offer resources to historically Black colleges and universities, and CEO Krishna backed specific legislative recommendations for Congress to address racial justice. The company’s “dedication to diversity seems to be consistently reflected in programs and initiatives, rather than just in statements of support,” an employee said. “Actions follow words in meaningful ways.”

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: International Business Machines’ big news in 2020 was the promotion of 30-year company executive Arvind Krishna to the CEO job, succeeding Ginni Rometty. IBM stock has been in a long swoon since 2013, even as the overall market has rocketed; the company needs a revised strategy, and Krishna has wasted little time pursuing one. In October 2020, he announced plans to spin off the business that manages IT infrastructure for other companies—IBM stock rose on the news—and he has been acquiring smaller businesses to build up IBM’s strength in cloud software for business automation. His strategic direction is no surprise; he had been following it even before he was CEO, championing IBM’s acquisition of the Red Hat enterprise software firm in 2019. Judging his success so far is difficult because the pandemic muddied comparisons with past performance.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: In 2019 IBM took the most dramatic step yet in its years-long project of adapting to a fast-changing tech environment, one in which Big Blue's historic dominance has been steadily eroded. In its largest acquisition ever, IBM spent $34 billion to buy Red Hat, the main distributor of the open-source operating system Linux. But progress on the company's top priorities—cloud computing, social engagement, mobile devices, and data analytics—has remained frustratingly slow, with revenue shrinking by 3% in 2019. This spring, however, the venerable computer giant got a new leader to take it forward. In April 2020, Arvind Krishna took the reins as CEO from Ginny Rometty, who had been serving in the role since 2012 and who remains executive chairman.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: In 2019 IBM took the most dramatic step yet in its years-long project of adapting to the fast-changing tech environment. It bought Red Hat, the main distributor of the open-source operating system Linux, paying $34 billion in its largest acquisition ever. But progress on CEO Ginni Rometty’s top priorities—cloud computing, social engagement, mobile devices, and data analytics—remained frustratingly slow. Revenue shrank; IBM’s Fortune 500 rank has declined every year for over a decade. In January 2020 the company announced that Rometty would step down after eight years as CEO, to be succeeded by longtime executive Arvind Krishna, who took over in April.
